title: Chicken Shawarma Rice Bowls
subtitle: warm-spiced chicken thighs over jasmine rice with cucumber, tomato and a creamy garlic sauce: shawarma-shop flavour, no heat
imageAlt: Sliced golden spiced chicken over rice with cucumber, tomato and garlic sauce in a white bowl on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: The spices are warm, not hot: cumin, paprika, a little turmeric and cinnamon. No chili.
Start the rice first; it's ready when the chicken is.

items.name: lemons
items.note: juiced, for the chicken and sauce

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Juice the lemon. Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp of the oil, 1 tbsp of the lemon juice, the cumin, paprika, garlic powder, turmeric, cinnamon, salt and pepper. Let it sit while the rice cooks, up to 30 minutes.

steps.title: Garlic sauce
steps.text: Stir the sour cream, mayonnaise, grated garlic, the other 1 tbsp lemon juice and the salt together. Chill until serving.

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.text: Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook the thighs 5–6 minutes a side, until well browned and 74°C (165°F) in the thickest part. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.

steps.title: Chop
steps.text: While the chicken cooks, dice the cucumber and tomatoes.

steps.title: Build the bowls
steps.text: Rice in each bowl, then the sliced chicken, cucumber and tomato, with a big spoon of garlic sauce.

fixIt.fix: The pan was too hot. Drop to medium once the first side has browned.
Pat it dry and don't move it for the first 4 minutes; crowding makes it steam, so use 2 batches if needed.
Raw garlic mellows after 15 minutes in the fridge; make it first.

saleTip: Boneless thighs at No Frills drop to about $11–13/kg on sale; English cucumbers are often 2 for $3.
swap: Chicken breast: same amount, pounded to an even 2 cm and cooked 4–5 minutes a side to 74°C (165°F).
leftovers: Pack the chicken and rice together and the cucumber, tomato and sauce in a separate container so they stay fresh.
doneness: Chicken thighs at 74°C (165°F) in the thickest part (Health Canada, poultry pieces). Reheat leftovers to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested home-style chicken shawarma methods (Canadian Living, Serious Eats): thighs in a warm cumin-paprika-turmeric marinade, pan-seared, with a garlic sauce; chili left out.
prepAhead: Season the chicken up to 1 day ahead; keep covered in the fridge.
The garlic sauce keeps 3 days in the fridge.
reheat: Chicken and rice covered in the microwave 2 minutes with a splash of water, until 74°C (165°F). Add the cold toppings after.

basic.note: Cumin, paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper, and a simple sour-cream garlic sauce.

stepNotes.1: Basic: skip the turmeric and cinnamon.
stepNotes.2: Basic: sour cream, garlic, lemon and salt; no mayonnaise.

fancy.note: Warm pitas on the side and a quick pickled onion.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: first toss the red onion with the vinegar, sugar and salt; it's pink and tangy by serving time.

addSteps.title: Warm the pitas
addSteps.text: Warm the pitas in a dry skillet 30 seconds a side and serve alongside, with the pickled onions over the bowls.

plating: Rice on one side, chicken fanned beside it.
Cucumber and tomato in their own little piles.
Garlic sauce in a big swoosh, pickled onions on top.

why.0-0: Thighs stay juicy over high heat, the way shawarma meat does on the spit.
why.0-7: A pinch of cinnamon is the warm note that makes it taste like shawarma, not taco night.
why.1-1: Mayonnaise makes the garlic sauce smooth and rich, like toum, without hours of whisking.

funFact: Shawarma comes from the Turkish 'çevirme', meaning 'turning', for the slowly rotating spit.
